claim: Coval & Shumway (J. Finance 2001): zero-beta at-the-money S&P 500 index straddles lost about 3% per week on average.

evidence.quote: zero‐beta, at‐the‐money straddle positions produce average losses of approximately three percent per week.

claim: Beckmeyer, Branger & Gayda: retail traders lost on average about $184k per day in 0DTE SPX options (about $358k per day after May 2022), and about 60% of the losses came from transaction costs.

evidence.quote: While average daily retail losses were $184,000 for the entire sample, since May 16, 2022 (the introduction of a daily expiration calendar), daily retail losses grew to $358,000.
evidence.source_title: Retail Investors are in Love with Same Day Options (summary by the authors, WealthManagement)

evidence.quote: buyers of options pay the variance risk premium and have negative expected returns even before expenses
evidence.source_title: Retail Investors are in Love with Same Day Options

claim: Vilkov's study of static 0DTE SPX rules held to expiry (Sept 2016-Jan 2024) finds deep in-the-money call buys have a positive median return but a mean not distinguishable from zero, and that P&L is largely explained by realised skewness of the underlying.

evidence.quote: Some trades look profitable at the median, including buying deep in-the-money calls and selling out-of-the-money calls and puts
evidence.source_title: 0DTE options: tiny edge, huge distribution (Hull Tactical summary of Vilkov)

evidence.quote: much of the P&L of these strategies can be explained by realized skewness in the underlying index return

claim: Kaminski & Lo (J. Financial Markets 2014): on index futures, some stop-loss policies can raise expected return and lower volatility at longer sampling frequencies.

evidence.quote: At longer sampling frequencies, certain stop-loss policies can increase expected return while substantially reducing volatility, consistent with their objectives in practical applications.
evidence.source_title: When do stop-loss rules stop losses? (MIT DSpace abstract)

claim: Lei & Li (Financial Services Review): on individual US stocks, stop-loss rules neither reduce nor increase losses relative to buy-and-hold; trailing stops reduce risk.

evidence.quote: Our results indicate that these strategies neither reduce nor increase investors' losses relative to a buy-and-hold strategy once we extend security returns from past realizations to possible future paths.
evidence.source_title: The value of stop loss strategies (FSR)

evidence.quote: stop-loss thresholds of 5, 10 or 20 daily return standard deviations
evidence.source_title: CXO Advisory summary of Lei & Li
